pr.title: gh-140576: Fixed crash produced by lexer in case of dedented zero byte
pr.body:
<!--
Thanks for your contribution!
Please read this comment in its entirety. It's quite important.

# Pull Request title

It should be in the following format:

```
gh-NNNNNN: Summary of the changes made
```

Where: gh-NNNNNN refers to the GitHub issue number.

Most PRs will require an issue number. Trivial changes, like fixing a typo, do not need an issue.

# Backport Pull Request title

If this is a backport PR (PR made against branches other than `main`),
please ensure that the PR title is in the following format:

```
[X.Y] <title from the original PR> (GH-NNNNNN)
```

Where: [X.Y] is the branch name, for example: [3.13].

GH-NNNNNN refers to the PR number from `main`.

-->


<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-140576 -->
* Issue: gh-140576
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+Fixed crash in :func:`tokenize.generate_tokens` in case of
+specific incorrect input. Patch by Mikhail Efimov.

review_comments.body: When would we have `PyErr_Occurred()` here? because I try to read the code and I can't find the path that was responsible for setting the exception actually. The tests also show that the error is essentially when we end with a NUL bytes so could it be because of that?
Yeah even if this is true this pattern is wrong: There should be proper error habdling in whatever is failing to do so instead of a global catch-all
Ok, I'll rewrite this, thanks for the clarification.

IIUC `tok_nextc` may set an exception. In this case `c` willl have `EOF` value.
So, the change looks valid.

issue_comments.body:
I have to say that I'm in doubt about using `PyErr_Occurred()` at `lexer.c`.
I'll be grateful for a little guidance.

Thanks @efimov-mikhail for the PR, and @pablogsal for merging it 🌮🎉.. I'm working now to backport this PR to: 3.13, 3.14.
🐍🍒⛏🤖 I'm not a witch! I'm not a witch!
